name: PD-L1 expression
summary: PD-L1 protein expression by immunohistochemistry is the principal companion and complementary biomarker for PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in NSCLC and triple-negative breast cancer, but it is an imperfect, continuous and dynamic predictor.
biology: PD-L1 (CD274) is expressed on tumour and immune cells, often adaptively induced by interferon-gamma from infiltrating T cells. Binding to PD-1 on activated T cells delivers an inhibitory signal that limits effector function within the tumour microenvironment. Constitutive expression can also arise from oncogenic signalling or CD274 amplification (9p24.1).
alterations: Protein overexpression on tumour cells and/or immune cells

methods: Immunohistochemistry with assay-specific scoring: 22C3 and 28-8 (tumour proportion score), SP263 (tumour cells), SP142 (tumour cells and immune cells)
Combined positive score (CPS) with 22C3 in triple-negative breast cancer
testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumour tissue (histology preferred; cytology acceptable when validated)
testing.notes: Assays and scoring systems are not fully interchangeable; the companion assay and scoring algorithm tied to each drug and indication should be used. Expression is spatially and temporally heterogeneous and may change after prior therapy.

predictiveRelevance: NSCLC: PD-L1 tumour proportion score informs choice between immunotherapy monotherapy and chemo-immunotherapy in the absence of actionable drivers, and is relevant to adjuvant and perioperative immunotherapy decisions. TNBC: CPS by 22C3 selects patients for pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in advanced disease; in early TNBC, neoadjuvant pembrolizumab benefit is observed irrespective of PD-L1. SCLC and mesothelioma: PD-L1 is not used to select patients for immunotherapy. PD-L1 negativity does not exclude benefit, and high expression does not guarantee response.
resistance: Primary resistance associated with STK11/KEAP1 co-mutation and oncogene-driven NSCLC (EGFR, ALK)
Acquired resistance via loss of antigen presentation (B2M, HLA loss), JAK1/2 loss-of-function, and immunosuppressive microenvironment changes
